mentions.context_excerpt: Converting CAD files to OpenUSD is a critical step in the physical AI pipeline — transforming engineering data into simulation-ready assets that developers can use to build, test and validate robots in physically accurate virtual environments.

mentions.access_constraints: public no-login Internet Archive replay; original publisher copyright retained; no republication grant inferred
mentions.context_excerpt: Companies including FANUC and Fauna Robotics are using this seamless CAD-to-OpenUSD workflow to speed up robotic system design and validation.

mentions.access_constraints: public no-login Internet Archive replay; original publisher copyright retained; no republication grant inferred
mentions.context_excerpt: KION , working with Accenture and Siemens, is using this blueprint to build large-scale warehouse digital twins that train and test fleets of NVIDIA Jetson-based autonomous forklifts for GXO, the world’s largest pure-play contract logistics provider.

mentions.access_constraints: public no-login Internet Archive replay; original publisher copyright retained; no republication grant inferred
mentions.context_excerpt: ABB Robotics , FANUC , KUKA and Yaskawa, which have a combined global install base of over 2 million robots, are using NVIDIA Omniverse libraries and NVIDIA Isaac simulation frameworks to validate complex robot applications and production lines through physically accurate digital twins . These companies have also integrated NVIDIA Jetson modules into their controllers to enable real-time AI inference.
